According to the indictment, the defendants, who were motivated by a combination of personal financial gain and allegiance to the Chinese MSS, adopted a surreptitious approach to conceal their theft of information, which entailed encrypting compromised data into RAR files, reconfiguring file names, extensions, and system timestamps to obscure detection, and secreting sensitive documents and programs in deceptively innocuous locations on victim networks, including "recycle bins", as a means to effectively disguise the unauthorized removal of data from these systems.

The defendants, with motivations rooted in both personal enrichment and loyalty to the Chinese MSS, executed a covert strategy to evade detection, which included encrypting pilfered data into RAR files, renaming and re-extending files and documents to obfuscate their origins, adjusting system timestamps to eliminate traces of their activities, and tactically concealing sensitive programs and documents within seemingly benign locations on compromised networks, such as the "recycle bins", ultimately aimed at disguising the unauthorized extraction of information from victim systems, as outlined in the indictment.
